 News › News News › UPSC Mains Result 2026 name list PDF out at upsc.gov.in: Download shortlisted candidates list, check… UPSC Mains Result 2026 name list PDF out at upsc.gov.in: Download shortlisted candidates list, check names and roll numbers
 Adhya Sarna Updated: Nov 6, 2026, 07:24 IST UPSC 2026 Mains results out The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) declared the result of the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026 on November 5, 2026. The result was published on the Commission's official website, upsc.gov.in . The written examination was conducted from August 21 to 30, 2026. 
 The result is released as a PDF, available both roll-number-wise and name-wise, and it identifies the candidates shortlisted for the Personality Test, the final stage of selection.
 UPSC result 2026 key figures 
 A total of 13,343 candidates qualified in the Preliminary Examination and became eligible to appear for the Mains. Of these, 2,526 have now been shortlisted for the interview. The examination is being conducted against an estimated 933 vacancies, which are subject to change.
 Comparatively, in 2025, 14,161 candidates qualified for the Mains, 2,736 were called for an interview, and 958 were finally selected. In 2024, 2,845 candidates were shortlisted against 1,056 vacancies, and 1,009 were eventually selected. The current shortlist is therefore smaller than in recent years, in line with the lower number of vacancies. It is also closer to the 2022 figures, when 2,529 candidates reached the interview stage against 1,011 vacancies.
 UPSC result 2026: How to access the result 
 Candidates may view the result without login credentials. They should visit upsc.gov.in, open the Examination menu, and select the Written Results section. The notification for the Civil Services (Main) Examination 2026 appears under ‘What's New’. Once the PDF is open, a candidate can locate their roll number using the search function on a computer or mobile device. Candidates are advised to download and retain a copy for reference.
 Download PDF here. 
 UPSC result 2026: Cut-off marks 
 The result PDF lists only the roll numbers of qualified candidates. It does not state individual marks or cut-off scores. UPSC's established practice is to publish marks, category-wise cut-offs and answer keys only after the entire examination cycle has concluded and the final result has been declared. Reports on the Prelims result for this cycle likewise noted that UPSC has stated that the marks, cut-off marks and answer keys would be released at a later stage.
 Candidates should therefore regard any cut-off figures circulating before then as unofficial estimates, not as authoritative data.
 Immediate steps for shortlisted candidates 
 Shortlisted candidates must complete several formalities in the coming weeks.
 First, they must submit the Detailed Application Form II (DAF-II) within the 15-day window announced by the Commission. This includes updating educational qualifications, correspondence details and employment information. 
 Final-year students must also upload their qualifying degree certificate.
 Second, candidates must submit their order of preference for services such as the Indian Administrative Service, Indian Police Service, Indian Foreign Service and Indian Revenue Service, along with their preferences for State cadres. These choices carry real weight, as allocation depends on final rank, category and the availability of vacancies.
 Third, candidates are required to complete the online Attestation Form of the Department of Personnel and Training through cseplus.nic.in within the prescribed deadline. They should also keep original certificates relating to education, date of birth, category and any benchmark disability ready for verification. Verification is conducted at Dholpur House, New Delhi, and candidates must follow all instructions issued by the UPSC and the DoPT.
 The e-Summon Letter for the interview will be made available on the UPSC website once the schedule and board allocation are announced.
 Preparing for the Personality Test 
 The Personality Test is intended to assess a candidate's suitability for a career in public service. It evaluates mental alertness, clarity of expression, balance of judgement, and intellectual and moral integrity. It is not a test of specialised knowledge. Candidates are advised to analyse their DAF thoroughly, since questions are frequently drawn from a candidate's background, education, hobbies and work experience. Regular revision of national and international current affairs, together with mock interviews, can help build confidence and composure. Attention to physical and mental well-being during this period is equally important.
